content: 1. Administer cefditoren at a dose of 200 mg orally once daily. For end-stage conditions, dosing has not been established. It is recommended to take the medication with meals to enhance absorption. Cefditoren is effective against pathogens such as Haemophilus influenzae, Haemophilus parainfluenzae, Streptococcus pneumoniae, and Moraxella catarrhalis. It is also indicated for pharyngitis/tonsillitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes and skin infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. 2. The safety and efficacy of cefditoren in children under 12 years of age have not been established. For children over 12 years, dosing is the same as for adults. 3. Cefditoren reduces the effectiveness of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is contraindicated to administer live bacterial vaccines during antibiotic therapy. Wait until the antibiotic course is completed before administering live vaccines. 4. Cefditoren interacts with the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of systemic antibiotics with the cholera vaccine, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 5. Cefditoren decreases the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibiotics may reduce the effectiveness of these products. Complete the antibiotic regimen 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 6. Aluminum hydroxide reduces the absorption of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of amikacin. Cephalosporins, including cefditoren, may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Cefditoren decreases the efficacy of atezolizumab, a checkpoint inhibitor, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Azithromycin reduces the efficacy of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like azithromycin may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents like cefditoren. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Calcium carbonate reduces the absorption of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of gentamicin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cefditoren decreases the efficacy of nivolumab, a checkpoint inhibitor, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Sodium bicarbonate reduces the absorption of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of streptomycin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tetracycline reduces the efficacy of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like tetracycline may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents like cefditoren. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of tobramycin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of kanamycin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of plazomicin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of neomycin. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity of voclosporin. Coadministration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Cefditoren increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Cefditoren increases the effects of choline magnesium trisalicylate by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Cefditoren increases the nephrotoxicity of furosemide through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction may increase the risk of nephrotoxicity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Cefditoren increases the effects of willow bark by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 26. Famotidine reduces the absorption of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ibuprofen/famotidine reduces the absorption of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Demeclocycline reduces the efficacy of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like demeclocycline may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents like cefditoren. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Dexlansoprazole reduces the absorption of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cefditoren decreases the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors such as pembrolizumab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, sintilimab, and tislelizumab through unspecified interaction mechanisms. Coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cefditoren decreases the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cefditoren increases the effects of estrogen-containing oral contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. This interaction poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 33. Probenecid increases the levels of cefditoren by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Cefditoren decreases the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine and cholera vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of live bacterial vaccines with systemic antibiotics. Wait until the antibiotic course is completed before administering live vaccines.
